classification.difficultyReason: Select SSS, SAS or AAS, match vertices and calculate a missing angle where needed.

content.prompt: In each part write a congruence statement and give a reason.

spec.description: Two downward-pointing triangles in a paired row. Ordinary source blue strokes are rendered black.
spec.mathematics: CO=8 cm, CN=7 cm, ON=5 cm; GR=5 cm, GU=8 cm, RU=7 cm. Matching vertices are N↔R, O↔G, C↔U.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied vertices and lengths are visible.

answer.worked:
$NO=RG=5\text{ cm}$, $OC=GU=8\text{ cm}$ and $CN=UR=7\text{ cm}$.

Therefore $\triangle NOC\equiv\triangle RGU$ (SSS).

spec.description: Paired triangles, left pointing upward and right downward, with horizontal 11 cm sides. Ordinary source blue strokes are rendered black.
spec.mathematics: TE=AB=5 cm, TN=AP=11 cm and angle ETN=angle BAP=40 degrees.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied vertices, side lengths and angle values are visible.

answer.worked:
$ET=BA=5\text{ cm}$, $TN=AP=11\text{ cm}$ and $\angle ETN=\angle BAP=40^\circ$.

The equal angles are included between the matching equal sides, so $\triangle ETN\equiv\triangle BAP$ (SAS).

spec.description: Paired triangles, left pointing upward and right downward. All four printed angle givens are retained. Ordinary source blue strokes are rendered black.
spec.mathematics: NL=ST=10 cm; angle LNM=60 degrees, angle NML=50 degrees, angle SPT=50 degrees and angle PST=70 degrees.
spec.answerVisibility: Calculated angles and congruence conclusions are hidden.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\angle NLM&=180^\circ-60^\circ-50^\circ\\\angle NLM&=70^\circ.\end{align*}$$
Thus $\angle NLM=\angle TSP=70^\circ$, $\angle NML=\angle SPT=50^\circ$ and $LN=ST=10\text{ cm}$.

Therefore $\triangle LNM\equiv\triangle STP$ (AAS).
